Saturn V AS-506 en la plataforma 39A del: Saturn V AS-506 on Launch Complex 39A at Kennedy Space Center. On board: Armstrong, Collins and Aldrin.
Arrancan los cinco motores F-1 de la pri: The five F-1 engines of the S-IC first stage start up.
Se liberan los brazos de sujeción. 2.900: The hold-down arms release. 2,900 tonnes leave the pad.
El cohete gira de 90° a un azimut de vue: The rocket rolls from 90° to a flight azimuth of 72°.
El Saturn V supera la velocidad del soni: The Saturn V breaks the speed of sound at ~7.8 km altitude.
Max Q: el momento de mayor esfuerzo aero: Max Q: the moment of greatest aerodynamic stress.
La primera etapa agota su combustible a: The first stage runs out of propellant at 66 km altitude.
ABANDONADA: la S-IC cae al Atlántico (im: ABANDONED: the S-IC falls into the Atlantic (impact ~T+9 min, 630 km offshore).
Five J-2 engines on the second stage.
La torre de escape (LES) ya no es necesa: The launch escape tower (LES) is no longer needed.
ABANDONADA: la S-II también caerá al Atl: ABANDONED: the S-II will also fall into the Atlantic.
First burn of the third stage.
Órbita de aparcamiento de 191 km, 88 min: 191 km parking orbit, 88 minutes per revolution.
La S-IVB se enciende de nuevo durante 5: The S-IVB fires again for 5 min 47 s.
Columbia se separa; se abren los paneles: Columbia separates; the adapter panels (SLA) open.
Columbia gira 180° y se acopla con el LM: Columbia turns 180° and docks with the LM Eagle.
Columbia + Eagle pull away from the S-IVB.
ABANDONADA: la S-IVB usa la gravedad lun: ABANDONED: the S-IVB uses lunar gravity to escape into orbit around the Sun.
Único ajuste de rumbo necesario en la id: The only course correction needed on the way out (MCC-2).
A partir de aquí manda la gravedad de la: From here on, the Moon's gravity takes over.
Encendido del motor SPS detrás de la Lun: SPS engine burn behind the Moon, out of contact with Earth.
Órbita casi circular de unos 100 x 120 k: Nearly circular orbit of about 100 x 120 km.
\"The Eagle has wings\": Eagle se separa: "The Eagle has wings": Eagle separates from Columbia.
Eagle baja su órbita a 15 km de altura m: Eagle lowers its orbit to a 15 km low point.
Ignición del motor de descenso a 15 km d: Descent engine ignition at 15 km altitude and 1.7 km/s.
Eagle rota para que el radar de aterriza: Eagle rolls so the landing radar can see the surface.
Sobrecarga del computador. Houston: \"We: Computer overload. Houston: "We're go on that alarm".
El computador apunta a una zona llena de: The computer is heading for a boulder field next to West crater.
Armstrong toma el control y vuela más al: Armstrong takes control and flies past the boulder field.
La etapa de ascenso parte. La etapa de d: The ascent stage lifts off. The descent stage stays forever.
Abandonada en órbita lunar tras el reenc: Abandoned in lunar orbit after the rendezvous
Base Tranquilidad, aún se usa para medir: Tranquility Base, still used to measure the Earth-Moon distance
Masa aproximada de Eagle al inicio de la: Approximate mass of Eagle at the start of P64; the fuel gives ~4 min of hovering
T-9,1 s (el 'zero' del locutor cae en T-: T-9.1 s (the announcer's 'zero' falls on T-0; 'liftoff' at T+2.4; 'roll program' at T+13)
Ignición de los F-1 (T-8,9 s); en Marte,: F-1 ignition (T-8.9 s); for Mars, Delta II ignition
Al llegar al espacio (~100 km, paso a la: On reaching space (~100 km, switch to the control room)
Contacto con la superficie (Luna o llega: Surface contact (Moon, or arrival at Mars)
El primer rover en Marte: 10,6 kg y seis: The first rover on Mars: 10.6 kg and six wheels. It drove about 100 m around its lander, renamed the Carl Sagan Memorial Station. It is still parked in Ares Vallis.
Diseñado para 90 soles, trabajó más de s: Designed for 90 sols, it worked for more than six years. In 2009 it got stuck in soft sand at 'Troy'; since then it has been a motionless monument in Gusev.
Recorrió más de 45 km en casi 15 años. U: It drove more than 45 km in almost 15 years. A global dust storm covered its solar panels in 2018 and it never woke up.
Excavó hielo de agua cerca del polo nort: It dug up water ice near the north pole. The Martian winter covered it in CO2 frost and crushed its solar panels.
Lander Phoenix (paneles rotos por el hie: Phoenix lander (panels broken by the ice)
NASA (Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, LRO,: NASA (Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, LRO, NSSDCA, JPL), ISRO, JPL Goldstone radar (2016), J. Meador (2021). Orbits are drawn with compressed altitude and illustrative orientation; surface positions are approximate.
S-IVB del Apollo 11 (3.ª etapa del Satur: Apollo 11's S-IVB (Saturn V 3rd stage): it swung past the Moon and ended up orbiting the Sun.
Paneles del adaptador SLA: espacio cislu: SLA adapter panels: cislunar space / solar orbit.
Etapa de ascenso del Apollo 10 «Snoopy»:: Apollo 10's ascent stage "Snoopy": orbiting the Sun.
Tras devolver a Armstrong y Aldrin a Col: After returning Armstrong and Aldrin to Columbia it was abandoned in lunar orbit on July 21, 1969. It was always assumed to have crashed, but a 2021 study (James Meador) concludes its orbit may have remained stable: it could still be there.
La primera misión lunar de la India. Se: India's first lunar mission. Contact was lost on August 29, 2009; in 2016 NASA's Goldstone radar found it again, still in its polar orbit at about 200 km.
En servicio. Fotografió desde órbita los: In service. From orbit it photographed the Apollo sites: you can see the descent stages, the rovers and even the footpaths.
Orbitador en servicio; su lander Vikram: Orbiter in service; its Vikram lander crashed in 2019.
South Korean lunar orbiter in service.
20 de julio de 1969: Eagle se posó en el: July 20, 1969: Eagle landed in the Sea of Tranquility. The descent stage served as a launch pad and stayed forever.
Sirvió de plataforma de lanzamiento para: It served as the launch pad for the ascent stage. One leg carries the plaque signed by the three astronauts and President Nixon.
Aldrin vio cómo la derribaba el chorro d: Aldrin saw the engine blast knock it over at liftoff.
Registró sismos lunares y hasta los paso: It recorded moonquakes and even the astronauts' footsteps. It stopped responding in August 1969.
Sigue funcionando: los observatorios tod: Still working: observatories still fire laser pulses at it to measure the Earth-Moon distance to the millimeter.
La que transmitió en directo la caminata: The one that broadcast the moonwalk live; it was left on its tripod.
Para ahorrar peso en el despegue se tira: To save weight for liftoff, the backpacks, boots and other items were thrown out of the hatch.
Disco con mensajes de buena voluntad de: A disc with goodwill messages from 73 countries, an Apollo 1 patch and medals honoring Gagarin and Komarov.
Armstrong caminó hasta su borde (~60 m a: Armstrong walked to its rim (~60 m east): the farthest excursion of Apollo 11.
Sonda de la NASA que se posó en el mismo: NASA probe that landed in the same sea on September 11, 1967, almost two years before Eagle.
El Ranger 8 se estrelló a propósito el 2: Ranger 8 crashed on purpose on February 20, 1965 after sending thousands of photos of the area where Apollo 11 would later land.
Intrepid aterrizó con precisión a unos 1: Intrepid made a pinpoint landing about 180 m from a probe that had been there for two and a half years: Surveyor 3.
La etapa de ascenso se estrelló después: The ascent stage was later crashed on purpose so the seismometers would record the impact.
Still standing according to LRO photos.
Sismómetro, magnetómetro y otros experim: Seismometer, magnetometer and other experiments powered by a nuclear generator (RTG). All ALSEPs were switched off on September 30, 1977.
Llegó en abril de 1967. Conrad y Bean le: It arrived in April 1967. Conrad and Bean cut off its camera and other parts and brought them back to Earth to study the effect of 31 months on the Moon.
La primera misión con rover lunar. El LR: The first mission with a lunar rover. LRV-1 was left parked east of the lunar module.
Recorrió unos 28 km. Se dejó aparcado (p: It drove about 28 km. It was left parked (approximate position) with its TV camera pointed at the lunar module to film the liftoff.
Pequeña estatuilla de aluminio y una pla: A small aluminum figurine and a plaque with the names of 14 astronauts and cosmonauts who died.
Apagada desde 1977. Su retrorreflector,: Switched off since 1977. Its retroreflector, larger than Apollo 11's, is still in use.
La última vez que un ser humano pisó la: The last time a human walked on the Moon (December 1972).
Lleva una placa que conmemora el fin de: It carries a plaque marking the end of humanity's first explorations of the Moon.
Recorrió unos 36 km; quedó aparcado al e: It drove about 36 km; it was left parked east of the LM (approximate position) to film the liftoff.
Noviembre de 1970: el primer rover que r: November 1970: the first rover to drive across another world, remotely controlled from the USSR.
Bajó al rover por unas rampas; quedó en: It lowered the rover down a pair of ramps; it stayed at the landing site.
Funcionó hasta septiembre de 1971. El LR: It worked until September 1971. LRO found it in 2010, and that same year its retroreflector bounced laser pulses back to Earth again.
Etapa de descenso de Antares, ALSEP y el: Antares descent stage, ALSEP and the MET hand cart. Alan Shepard hit two golf balls here.
Etapa de descenso de Orion, el rover LRV: Orion descent stage, the LRV-2 rover and a family photo left by Charlie Duke.
El primer objeto humano en llegar a la L: The first human-made object to reach the Moon: it crashed on September 13, 1959.
Lander chino y su rover Yutu, que quedó: Chinese lander and its Yutu rover, which came to a stop a few meters away.
Primer aterrizaje cerca del polo sur lun: First landing near the lunar south pole. Both went to sleep in September 2023 and never woke up.
El primer aterrizaje en la cara oculta,: The first landing on the far side, linked through a relay satellite.
1.ª etapa y propulsores GEM del Delta II: Delta II 1st stage and GEM boosters: fell into the Atlantic.
2.ª etapa del Delta II: se quedó en órbi: Delta II 2nd stage: stayed in Earth orbit and eventually reentered.
3.ª etapa (Star 48): siguió a la nave y: 3rd stage (Star 48): followed the spacecraft and ended up orbiting the Sun.
Etapa de crucero: llevó la cápsula duran: Cruise stage: it carried the capsule during the months-long trip and separated minutes before atmospheric entry, where it burned up. It did not stay in orbit.
Cápsula de entrada: el escudo térmico, l: Entry capsule: the heat shield, backshell and parachute ended up scattered across the surface near the site.
Estudiaba cómo Marte perdió su atmósfera: It studied how Mars lost its atmosphere. It stopped communicating on December 6, 2025, spinning unexpectedly; NASA declared the mission over in June 2026.
Se perdió en noviembre de 2006. Se calcu: Lost in November 2006. It is expected to stay in orbit until the mid-2040s.
La primera misión de la India a Marte. S: India's first mission to Mars. It ran out of fuel and battery power and lost contact in 2022.
La primera nave que orbitó otro planeta: The first spacecraft to orbit another planet (November 14, 1971). Switched off in 1972; it was predicted to fall around 2022, but no one has confirmed it.
Funcionó hasta 1980. Su destino exacto e: It worked until 1980. Its exact fate is uncertain (approximate orbit).
Llegó el mismo mes que Mariner 9. Se pre: It arrived the same month as Mariner 9. It is presumed to still be in orbit, like the Mars 3 and Mars 5 orbiters.
Se perdió en marzo de 1989 mientras se a: Lost in March 1989 while approaching the moon Phobos.
La nave más longeva en otro planeta. Ret: The longest-lived spacecraft at another planet. It relayed most of Spirit's and Opportunity's data. It keeps working on very little fuel.
Su cámara HiRISE fotografió los landers,: Its HiRISE camera photographed the landers, parachutes and heat shields on this very list.
En servicio. Su lander Beagle 2 se dio p: In service. Its Beagle 2 lander was given up for lost until it was found in 2015.
En servicio. Su lander de prueba Schiapa: In service. Its Schiaparelli test lander crashed on landing.
4 de julio de 1997: Pathfinder rebotó so: July 4, 1997: Pathfinder bounced on its airbags and opened its petals. Sojourner, the first rover on Mars, rolled down a ramp.
Lander Pathfinder · Estación Memorial Ca: Pathfinder lander · Carl Sagan Memorial Station
Último contacto: 27 de septiembre de 199: Last contact: September 27, 1997. The deflated airbags are still around the petals.
10,6 kg y unos 100 m recorridos alrededo: 10.6 kg and about 100 m driven around the lander. When the lander went silent, it was left waiting for commands that never came.
La primera roca marciana analizada por u: The first Martian rock analyzed by a rover.
Protegió la cápsula a más de 7 km/s dura: It protected the capsule at more than 7 km/s during entry.
Se soltaron segundos antes de inflar los: They were released seconds before the airbags inflated.
Diseñado para 90 soles, Spirit trabajó m: Designed for 90 sols, Spirit worked for more than six years at Gusev.
Bautizada en memoria de la tripulación d: Named in memory of the crew of the Space Shuttle Columbia.
En 2009 sus ruedas se hundieron en arena: In 2009 its wheels sank into soft sand next to Home Plate. Last contact: March 22, 2010.
Opportunity cayó dentro de un cráter de: Opportunity landed inside a 22 m crater, Eagle: a "hole in one" from 456 million km away.
Still at the bottom of Eagle crater.
Junto al escudo encontró este meteorito: Next to the shield it found this metallic meteorite: the first one identified on another planet (January 2005).
Una tormenta de polvo global cubrió sus: A global dust storm covered its panels in 2018. Last contact: June 10, 2018.
Phoenix excavó hielo de agua cerca del p: Phoenix dug up water ice near the north pole. Winter buried it in CO₂ frost.
Last contact: November 2, 2008. In 2010 the HiRISE camera saw that winter ice had bent or broken its solar panels.
Al excavar apareció hielo blanco que se: Digging exposed white ice that sublimated within a few days.
20 de julio de 1976: el primer aterrizaj: July 20, 1976: the first fully successful landing on Mars.
Septiembre de 1976. Fotografió escarcha: September 1976. It photographed frost in winter.
Funcionó hasta abril de 1980, cuando fal: It worked until April 1980, when its batteries failed.
InSight escuchó el interior de Marte: re: InSight listened to the interior of Mars: it recorded more than a thousand marsquakes.
El polvo cubrió sus paneles; último cont: Dust covered its panels; last contact: December 15, 2022.
Detectó sismos marcianos y los impactos: It detected marsquakes and meteorite impacts.
El suelo no le daba agarre y nunca logró: The soil gave it no grip and it never managed to dig to the planned depth.
Rover en servicio. Cerca quedaron su eta: Rover in service. Its descent stage (sky crane), which crashed on purpose, and its heat shield lie nearby.
Ingenuity, el primer helicóptero en otro: Ingenuity, the first helicopter on another planet, flew 72 times. It was grounded in January 2024 and is still there; NASA left it storing data in its memory for whoever comes next. Perseverance keeps exploring far from here.
1,8 kg. Diseñado para 5 vuelos de prueba: 1.8 kg. Designed for 5 test flights, it made 72. On its last landing (January 18, 2024) its blades were damaged and it could no longer take off.
Perseverance fotografió un fragmento de: Perseverance photographed a piece of blade about 15 m from the helicopter (approximate position).
Rover de la NASA que llegó en febrero de: NASA rover that arrived in February 2021 carrying Ingenuity under its belly. It collects rock samples in sealed tubes.
Ingenuity los fotografió desde el aire e: Ingenuity photographed them from the air in April 2022.
Rover chino. Entró en hibernación en may: Chinese rover. It went into hibernation in May 2022 and never woke up.
Lander británico dado por perdido; en 20: British lander given up for lost; in 2015 it was found in HiRISE images with its panels half open.
Lander de prueba europeo que se estrelló: European test lander that crashed after shutting off its engines too early.
El primer aterrizaje suave en Marte (URS: The first soft landing on Mars (USSR): it transmitted for only a few seconds.
